correctness.rationale: For fixed even n>=4, Fourier eigenvalues 2cos(theta+2pi k/n) give degeneracies precisely k and n-1-k at theta*=pi/n and exact antipodal destructive interference; the Cesaro projection sum yields (J+I-P)/n. Every allowed nonzero detuning splits eigenvalues; the sine-factor identity bounds all unequal gaps below (8/pi)sin(pi/n)|delta|. Termwise integration and |F_T|<=2/(T gap) give the stated all-entry upper threshold. Duhamel and the exactly dark antipodal entry give tau>=sqrt(3/(8n))/|delta|. Only split pairs survive at T=s/|delta|, yielding the finite sinc profile; limits s->0,infinity follow. Independent direct Fourier calculations reproduced resonant matrices and n=4,6,8 crossover values (approximately 0.1495613, 0.0901648, 0.0671991 at s=.75); scaled finite-delta discrepancies below 2e-6. Claims are for fixed n, uniform time averaging, not optimizing finite-size constants.

originality.rationale: PASS with residual risk: Levine et al. Theorem 5 proves the qualitative J/n limit for any simple-spectrum cyclic Hermitian circulant, hence covers detuned infinite-time uniformity. This claim does not relabel that as new: it identifies the exact half-flux degeneracy, the inverse-detuning finite observation-time bottleneck, and the explicit antipodal sinc crossover. Earlier real-symmetric cycle and nonnegative-weight comparisons do not cover the complex magnetic flux. A universal nearly degenerate spectral perturbation theorem could imply aspects of the profile; no exact covering statement was found in current comparisons.
residual_risks: The constants in tau bounds are not optimal; fixed-n exponent only.
A general spectral-resonance perturbation source could state an equivalent sinc profile; this was not ruled out exhaustively.

value.rationale: PASS: Half flux is a natural geometric interference boundary where the antipodal channel is dark. The sharp divergence exponent for finite observation times and the explicit critical scaling profile quantify noncommuting flux and time limits, beyond the known simple-spectrum infinite-time mixing assertion.
